rationale: This is a one-token edit of the archive's "Revenue Servicing Capacity of Research Firms" (sale→sale−cogs in the same numerator, same gate, same scaling), i.e. a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the gross-profit leg is additionally a near-direct rediscovery of Novy-Marx gross profitability re-scaled by liabilities.

Both legs are recycled from the archive, but the pairing is a genuine and internally consistent attempt to resolve the documented slope/alpha disagreement (large-alpha composition tilt × the only conditioner with a strong Fama-MacBeth slope), and the signed-difference × positive-conditioner form does behave monotonically in the claimed direction.

The stated target — firms high on *both* leverage and cash coverage — cannot be isolated by SUMRANK, which assigns the same score to a low-leverage/high-coverage firm and a high-leverage/low-coverage firm, so the expression does not compute the hypothesis; separately, loading positively on raw leverage contradicts the distress-risk evidence and is asserted rather than identified.

Because the R&D add-back is zero for most of the cross-section, the signal reduces to pretax-earnings-to-liabilities — an Altman/Ohlson-style profitability-over-leverage ratio and a well-known anomaly composite — so any result will be dominated by the standard profitability effect rather than the intangible-expensing wedge the theme is trying to isolate.

Scaling goodwill by liabilities makes the signal mechanically high for acquisitive firms with *little* debt, which is the opposite of the "illusory asset coverage supporting obligations" story (goodwill/assets or goodwill/equity would match the hypothesis), and the resulting univariate goodwill-intensity sort is close to already-documented goodwill/intangible-intensity effects.

target_name: Chronic Cash Burn in Research Firms
rationale: A defensible and previously untested attempt to isolate the genuine-fragility side within the intangible population using a hard, non-accrual persistence criterion, though the five-valued indicator count is coarse enough to create lumpy, tie-heavy portfolios and it overlaps conceptually with the archive's chronic-loss-years signal.
